This application is filed under Section 482 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (for short, BNSS), seeking pre- arrest bail.

2. The applicant is the accused No.1 in Crime No.1120/2024 of Medical College Police Station,
Thiruvananthapuram District.

Medical College Police Station,
Thiruvananthapuram District
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The offences alleged are punishable under Sections 406 and 420 r/w Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code.

3. The prosecution case, in short, is that accused Nos. 1 to 4 with a common intention to deceive the defacto complainant and to have unlawful enrichment, offered to him that they will appoint him as the head of Surgical Gastroenterology Department of a new Multi Specialty Hospital, make him a share holder of that hospital, also offered to him that they will manage to appoint him as the Director of All India Institute of Medical Science, thereby caused him to deliver him a total sum of Rs.3,02,50,000/- by way of bank account transfer to the account of accused Nos.2 and 3 and payment in cash.

entities.text: All India Institute of Medical Science
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The defacto complainant acted in terms of the assurance 2026:KER:19460 given by the applicant and as advised by him.

The accused after receiving the amount did not complete the construction of Multi Specialty Hospital at Dharward in Karnataka, not obeyed their undertaking,
did not return the amount received from the defacto complainant and thereby committed the offences.
4. I have heard Sri.Reginald Valsalan, the learned counsel for the applicant and Sri.M.C.Ashi, the learned Senior Public Prosecutor.
Perused the case diary.
5. The learned counsel for the applicant submitted that the applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the above crime.
The counsel further submitted that no materials are on record to connect the applicant with the alleged crime; hence, he is entitled to bail.

The learned Senior Public Prosecutor, on the other hand, submitted that the alleged incident occurred as part of the applicant's intentional criminal acts, and if he is released on bail at this stage, it will affect the course of the investigation.

sentences.text: It is true that the allegation against the applicant is serious in nature.
According to the prosecution, it was the applicant who introduced accused Nos.2 to 4 to the defacto 2026:KER:19460 complainant and it was at his instance money was given to accused Nos.2 to 4.
Admittedly, the applicant did not receive any money at all from the defacto complainant.
All the money was received by accused Nos.2 to 4.
Accused No.2 has approached this Court seeking pre-arrest bail and it was dismissed.
Thereafter, accused No.2 challenged the said order before the Hon'ble Supreme Court and the Hon'ble Supreme Court as per Annexure-A3 order granted pre-arrest bail to the accused No.2.

The prosecution objected the same before the Hon'ble Supreme Court stating that accused No.2 was the kingpin of the entire transaction and he was the person who had been defrauding people by collecting huge sum of money by making false promise.
Still, pre-arrest bail was granted to the accused No.2 by the Hon'ble Supreme Court,
Similarly, this Court as per Annexure-A4 order granted pre-arrest bail to the accused No.3.
Even though the defacto complainant challenged the said order before the Hon'ble Supreme Court, it ended in dismissal as seen from Annexure-A5 order of the Hon'ble Supreme Court.
In these circumstances, I am of the view that the applicant is also entitled for pre-arrest bail on the ground of 2026:KER:19460 parity.
For these reasons, I find this to be an appropriate case to grant pre-arrest bail to the applicant.

In the result, the application is allowed on the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall be released on bail in the event of his arrest on executing a bond for Rs.1,00,000/- (Rupees One lakh only) with two solvent sureties for the like sum each to the satisfaction of the arresting officer/investigating officer, as the case may be.
(ii) The applicant shall fully cooperate with the investigation, including subjecting himself to the deemed police custody for discovery, if any, as and when demanded.

(iii) The applicant shall appear before the investigating officer between 10.00 a.m.
and 11.00 a.m. every Saturday until further orders.
He shall also appear before the investigating officer as and when required.
(iv) The applicant shall not commit any offence of a like nature while on bail.

(v) The applicant shall not attempt to contact any of the prosecution witnesses,
directly or through any other person, or 2026:KER:19460 in any other way try to tamper with the evidence or influence any witnesses or other persons related to the investigation.
(vi) The applicant shall not leave the State of Kerala without the permission of the trial Court.
(vii) The application, if any, for deletion/modification of bail conditions or cancellation of bail on the grounds of violating the bail conditions shall be filed at the jurisdictional court.
